755	**Four designer annotations define real behaviour no AC mentions:**
756	1. Empty state still reserves the space "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors"

as a standard 198 item; only digital is special.

## 11.3 Cart-level-messages (SFCC-404) — NOT a simple banner

Shell: px 128, bg white, gap 4px between stacked messages, **min-h 52 reserved even when empty**,
`Page-level-message` w **476px** fixed, `Message-container` gap 8px,
**`touchTarget` 24x24 wrapping a 20px icon**, text `Default/body2` (Futura Round regular/400,
14px, lh 18px).

| Variant | Icon | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| Error | `Icon_close` | `text/error` **#9c0000** |
| Success | `Icon_tick` | `text/success` **#2d5a3d** |
| Warning | `Icon_info_solid` | `text/subtlest` **#969696** |

**Four designer annotations define real behaviour no AC mentions:**
1. Empty state still reserves the space "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors"
2. Errors **aggregate into one counted message** with a **live count that decrements** as the
   shopper resolves them; errors **always stay at the top** when stacked
3. Only **one success at a time**; container stays fixed, old fades out, new fades in
4. **Warnings are suppressed entirely** whenever an error or success is present

=> precedence: error (pinned, aggregated) > success (single-slot, crossfade) > warning (suppressed).
=> full ICU pluralisation: "There **is 1** item ... **requires** action" / "There **are 2** ...
   **require** action".
=> **This is a message aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions.** The
   "half a day" estimate given when deciding whether to pull 404 forward was wrong by a lot.
=> our interim Chakra toast **stacks** by default — a poorer stand-in than assumed, but still
   interim. Reinforces routing every message through one handler.

Copy found: "There is 1 item in your bag that requires action" · "An item in your bag has reached
maximum quantity" · "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" · "An item in your bag already exists
in Wishlist" · "Item added to Wishlist" (stacked — **drops the product name**)

## 11.4 *** DISCLOSURE COPY EXISTS — corrects a decided premise ***

The WARNINGS SHOWN state reads:
> **"An item in your bag has been reduced to the maximum allowed quantity"**

Two distinct max-quantity messages exist:
1. "has **reached** maximum quantity" — at the cap (CART MERGE state)
2. "has been **reduced to** the maximum allowed quantity" — **we changed your bag**

SFCC-250's ACs contain only #1. Disclosure was ruled out of scope **on my statement that no such
copy existed — that statement was wrong.** The decision stands unless Marcel revisits it, but the
premise was false and the copy is specced.

## 11.5 Cart-button-group (SFCC-275)

430x188. Button-group flex-col gap **16px** (space/400). All buttons **h 52**, px **32**

# PRD – Cart & Inventory

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Cart & Inventory" and "Order Management". Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---
---
- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

### Buffer stock
- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.
- Business users can set buffer stock via bulk upload (by category, colour, store view).
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when variant stock exceeds buffer threshold (CAI-026)
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when stock is above zero but at or below buffer threshold; Add to Bag disabled and back-in-stock capture presented (CAI-027)
- **OUT OF STOCK** also shown when variant stock is fully depleted; same disabled state and back-in-stock capture (CAI-028)
- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)
- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP (CAI-031)

### General availability vs. boutique stock
- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework, extended post-rework (found live in Storybook by Marcel, not by this
3	 * suite). Proves three stacked bugs are actually fixed TOGETHER, not just that the symbols were
4	 * added:
5	 *   1. `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` (base SFCC hook, unconditional
6	 *      `product.variants.filter(...)`) needs `variants` to be an array on the mock product.
7	 *   2. `useDerivedProduct` unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`, which throws without a
8	 *      real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
9	 *   3. `item-attributes.tsx`'s `useCurrentBasket()` call has its own separate transitive chain
10	 *      (`useSFPayments` -> `useAppOrigin` -> `useOrigin`) that calls the SDK's
11	 *      `useServerContext()` and destructures `res` from it unconditionally, before `useOrigin`'s
12	 *      own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res`) is reached. This
13	 *      file previously mocked `useCurrentBasket` away entirely, which hid this bug completely —
14	 *      unmocked now so this suite actually exercises the real chain. `ServerContext.Provider`
15	 *      with `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
16	 *      client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
17	 *
18	 * Deliberately does NOT use index.test.tsx's harness — that file mocks the whole
19	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks` barrel's `useDerivedProduct`, which would hide both
20	 * bugs this file exists to catch. This renders through the real, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` ->
21	 * `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` / `useSelectedStore` chain, with a real
22	 * `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
23	 *
24	 * `useMultiSite` and `useCurrency` are still mocked, for a reason that has nothing to do with
25	 * this build's own logic: `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts` (the barrel both
26	 * `MultiSiteProvider`/`CurrencyProvider` and `use-multi-site.js`/`use-currency.js` resolve
27	 * through) is a `.js` file containing inline JSX, which Vite's transform cannot parse as a
28	 * plain `.js` file — confirmed empirically (this file's first draft imported `MultiSiteProvider`
29	 * from that barrel directly and vitest failed at import-analysis on
30	 * `app/contexts/index.js:49`, not at any assertion). This is the same parse failure
31	 * item-variant/index.test.tsx's own docblock already documents and works around by mocking
32	 * `use-multi-site` instead of using a real `MultiSiteProvider`; extended here to `useCurrency`
33	 * for the same reason. `StoreLocatorProvider` itself is real: `use-selected-store.js` and
34	 * `store-locator-provider.jsx` both import `StoreLocatorContext` via that file's own direct path
35	 * (`.../app/contexts/store-locator-provider`), never through the barrel, so it never hits this
36	 * parse wall — confirmed by reading both files' imports, not assumed.
37	 *
38	 * Two more pragmatic mocks, both explained inline at their own `vi.mock`/`beforeEach`: `useStores`
39	 * (an unrelated dual-module-instance QueryClient issue, not this build's own code) and a
40	 * `window.matchMedia` polyfill (jsdom has none; item-price.tsx's `useBreakpointValue` needs it —
41	 * the same pre-existing gap and fix product-item/index.test.tsx's own `beforeEach` already uses).
42	 * Neither affects what this file actually proves: that a real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor and
43	 * an array-valued `variants` together stop the render from throwing.
44	 */
45	import React from 'react';
46	import { describe, test, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
47	import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
48	import { ChakraProvider } from '@chakra-ui/react';
49	import { IntlProvider } from 'react-intl';
50	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
51	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
52	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
53	import { StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts/store-locator-provider';
54	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
55	import theme from 'app/theme';
56	import ProductItem from '.';
57	
58	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site', () => ({
59	  default: vi.fn(() => ({ site: { id: 'ZimmermannAU' }, buildUrl: (path: string) => path })),
60	}));
61	
62	// Cannot use this factory's `importOriginal` here: it resolves the barrel itself
63	// (`app/hooks/index.js`), which re-exports `useCurrency` from `use-currency.js`, which imports
64	// `CurrencyContext` from the broken `app/contexts` barrel — so `importOriginal()` transitively
65	// hits the same parse wall as importing `MultiSiteProvider` does (confirmed empirically: this
66	// was the first thing tried here, and it failed at the identical `app/contexts/index.js:49`
67	// parse error). `vi.importActual` on `use-derived-product`'s own direct sub-path sidesteps it —
68	// that file's own dependency chain never touches `app/contexts` (confirmed by grepping it and
69	// every hook it imports).
70	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks', async () => {
71	  const { useDerivedProduct } = await vi.importActual<
72	    typeof import('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product')
73	  >('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product');
74	  return {
75	    useCurrency: () => ({ currency: 'AUD', setCurrency: vi.fn() }),
76	    useDerivedProduct,
77	  };
78	});
79	
80	// Same fix as product-item/index.test.tsx's own: PromoPopover imports the base SFCC icons
81	// barrel, which has a top-level side effect that throws under Vitest (testing.md's documented
82	// ZimmIcon gap, same root cause via a different import path).
83	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/promo-popover', () => ({
84	  default: ({ children }: { children?: React.ReactNode }) => <>{children}</>,
85	}));
86	
87	// SFCC-795 rework (ZimmInlineMessage's warning icon): ProductItem -> ZimmInlineMessage ->
88	// ZimmIcon -> the base SFCC icons barrel is a new static import chain as of this rework, hitting
89	// the identical top-level-side-effect crash the mock above already works around for
90	// PromoPopover's own path to that same barrel. Neither test below passes a `message` prop, so the
91	// icon never needs to render distinguishably — testing.md's own documented canonical form
92	// (`ZimmIcon: () => null`) applies directly, no props need forwarding.
93	vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({
94	  ZimmIcon: () => null,
95	}));
96	
97	// `useStores` is mocked too (in addition to usePromotions/useProducts/useProduct, needed for the
98	// same reason as product-item/index.test.tsx's own): the REAL `useSelectedStore` (unmocked, the
99	// actual thing this file proves doesn't throw) calls it internally, and the real `useStores` hit
100	// an unrelated environment issue here — `@tanstack/react-query`'s `useQueryClient()` not finding
101	// this file's own `QueryClientProvider` (a dual-module-instance style mismatch, not anything this
102	// build's own code controls). Mocking only `useStores` still exercises `useSelectedStore`'s own
103	// real body — including the `useContext(StoreLocatorContext)` throw-if-missing check this file
104	// exists to prove no longer throws — while sidestepping that unrelated plumbing issue.
105	vi.mock('@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react', async (importOriginal) => {
106	  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react')>();
107	  return {
108	    ...actual,
109	    usePromotions: () => ({ data: undefined }),
110	    useProducts: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
111	    useProduct: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
112	    useStores: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
113	    // Same dual-module-instance QueryClient issue as useStores above, surfacing here now that
114	    // useCurrentBasket (unmocked, see this file's own docblock) calls this for real internally.
115	    useCustomerBaskets: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
116	  };
117	});
118	
119	const storyQueryClient = new QueryClient({
120	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
121	});
122	
123	// `useStores` (called for real inside the real `useSelectedStore`, unmocked above) is left real
124	// too — it resolves with `enabled: false` (no selectedStoreId in this jsdom's empty
125	// localStorage), so it registers a disabled query and never actually fetches, matching
126	// index.stories.tsx's own documented reasoning for its inert CommerceApiProvider/proxy setup.
127	const renderWithStoryProviders = (ui: React.ReactElement) =>
128	  render(
129	    <ServerContext.Provider value={{}}>
130	      <ChakraProvider theme={theme}>
131	        <MemoryRouter>
132	          <QueryClientProvider client={storyQueryClient}>
133	            <CommerceApiProvider
134	              clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
135	              organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
136	              shortCode="storybook"
137	              siteId="ZimmermannAU"
138	              locale="en-AU"
139	              currency="AUD"
140	              proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
141	              redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
142	              disableAuthInit
143	              silenceWarnings
144	            >
145	              <StoreLocatorProvider config={{ defaultCountryCode: 'AU', defaultPostalCode: '2000' }}>
146	                <IntlProvider locale="en-AU" defaultLocale="en-AU">
147	                  {ui}
148	                </IntlProvider>
149	              </StoreLocatorProvider>
150	            </CommerceApiProvider>
151	          </QueryClientProvider>
152	        </MemoryRouter>
153	      </ChakraProvider>
154	    </ServerContext.Provider>,
155	  );
156	
157	// Mirrors index.stories.tsx's own MOCK_LINE_ITEM shape, including the round 2 `variants: []` fix.
158	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM = {
159	  itemId: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6',

162	  productName: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',
163	  name: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',
164	  price: 495,

174	    },

62	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
63	 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
65	 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
66	 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
67	 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
68	 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
69	 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
70	 *
71	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
72	 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
73	 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
74	 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
75	 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
76	 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
77	 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
78	 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
79	 *
80	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): `discountLabel` (optional, prop-driven) renders directly beneath the
81	 * stepper/price row: DOM order is stepper -> discountLabel -> message -> secondaryActions.
82	 * "Beneath the stepper" is sourced (session-notes.md line 394's own ticket-summary prose, and the
83	 * plan's own step 3.3 pass criterion 2 wording); placing it AHEAD of `message` specifically is
84	 * this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement — no citation
85	 * in session-notes.md sequences discountLabel relative to message (checked directly, not assumed),
86	 * and the pass criterion itself is satisfied by "beneath the stepper" alone regardless of order.
87	 * Chosen because a discount is a property of the line item's own state (always true or false for
88	 * that line), while `message` is closer to point-of-action feedback nearer the actions row — a
89	 * reasonable read, not a tested one. Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order.
90	 * Purely presentational, per session-notes.md §4's SFCC-795 decisions
91	 * ("Only the discount label is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired
92	 * when the promotions engine lands"): this component does not compute a discount percentage or
93	 * label itself; a caller supplies the already-resolved string once something upstream (the

102	 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
103	 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
104	 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).

139	type ProductItemProps = {

141	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
142	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
143	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
144	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
145	  /**
146	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
147	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
148	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
149	   */
150	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;

152	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
153	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;

155	  isRemoving?: boolean;
156	  pickupInStore?: boolean;

160	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
161	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
162	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
163	   */
164	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
165	  /**

167	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
168	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
169	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
170	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
171	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
172	   */
173	  message?: {
174	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
175	    text: string;
176	  };
177	  /**

179	   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
180	   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
181	   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
182	   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
183	   *
184	   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
185	   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
186	   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
187	   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
188	   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
189	   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
190	   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
191	   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
192	   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
193	   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
194	   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
195	   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac

199	   */

201	};

203	/**
204	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
205	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
206	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
207	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
208	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
209	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
210	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
211	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
212	 */
213	const ProductItem = ({
214	  product,
215	  primaryAction,
216	  secondaryActions,
217	  deliveryActions,
218	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
219	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
220	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
221	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
222	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
223	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
224	  showLoading = false,
225	  containerStyles = {},

227	  pickupInStore = false,

241	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
242	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
243	  return (
244	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
245	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>

247	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
248	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
249	            <CartItemVariantImage />

252	                <Stack spacing={1}>
253	                  <CartItemVariantName />
254	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
255	                  <HideOnDesktop>
256	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
257	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
258	                    </Box>
259	                  </HideOnDesktop>
260	                </Stack>
261	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
262	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
263	                )}
264	              </Flex>
265	
266	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
267	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
268	              )}
269

269	
270	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
271	                <Stack spacing={1}>
272	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
273	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
274	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
275	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
276	                    ) : (
277	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
278	                        product={product}
279	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
280	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
281	                        quantity={quantity}
282	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
283	                      />
284	                    ))}
285	                </Stack>

291	                </Stack>
292	              </Flex>

295	                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
296	                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
297	              {discountLabel && (

299	              )}

302	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction

304	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}

`dataTestId` provided overrides it and the default testid is then genuinely absent (proves no collision). **5. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx`** - Swapped the bespoke `` for ``, same conditional (`{discountLabel && (...)}`), same DOM position (still ahead of `message`). `Text` import kept — still used for the inventory-message block (line 309). - Rewrote the `discountLabel` prop's JSDoc and the top-of-file step-3.3 docblock paragraph to cite the real pulled node instead of the old `colourSize`-precedent/"no citation exists" claims, both now factually wrong. **6. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx` — verified, not edited.** Both existing `discountLabel` tests (omitted → no node; I searched that file directly (both a plain grep for "low-stock"/"low stock" and a full read of its actual `## 11.2 Cart Item` section, lines 710-740) — **it says nothing about low-stock at all.** The real, verifiable source for "no low-stock messaging in the cart" is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/cart.md:70` (CAI-030): "Low-stock indicator shown at size level — no quantity number displayed; not displayed in mini-cart or cart." The underlying rule is real and I haven't touched it — I widened the recipe to three variants, none of them low-stock. But the citation attached to that rule in the code was invented or drifted from something else, and I corrected it to the source I actually verified rather than perpetuate an unverifiable one, per this session's own citation rule. Flagging this because (a) it's exactly the class of thing you'd want ratified rather than silently rewritten, and (b) it's worth asking whether anything else in this build cited "session-notes.md §11.2" for a claim that section doesn't actually make. ## Judgement calls I made (not fully specified in the brief) - **`dataTestId` prop naming**: I checked for an existing pattern first — grepped every atom under `ui-kits/atoms/` for any existing testid-override convention. There isn't one; every other atom hardcodes its testid with no override. So `dataTestId?: string` (camelCase prop, mapped internally to the `data-testid` attribute, default `'zimm-inline-message'`) is a new convention, not a precedent I'm following. It wasn't in your file manifest, so I left it alone rather than deciding scope for you — noted here, not fixed. ## Verification `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, no output, no errors. `npm run test` (= `vitest run`, confirmed from `package.json`) — full suite, run once: **93 test files, 1311 tests, all passed**, including `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6) and the new/changed tests above. The `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` stderr lines are pre-existing jsdom/Chakra noise that appears across unrelated files too (e.g. `theme/index.test.tsx`, `product-view/index.test.tsx`) — not something this change introduced. ## Unverified gaps (mine) - No Storybook story added for the `success` variant (see judgement call above) — the atom's visual QA surface is now incomplete relative to its real variant set. - I did not run `coderabbit`/lint — not asked for in this pass's completion criteria (tsc + test only), and AGENTS.md's CodeRabbit step is for "before committing," which isn't this step. ## What Marcel is missing Nothing about this step's code, but a process observation: this is now a confirmed instance of a docblock citation that doesn't hold up when actually checked against the file it names (session-notes.md §11.2 for the low-stock rule). Given this codebase's own rule exists specifically because this has happened before, it may be worth a one-time sweep of other "session-notes.md §NN.N" citations in the cart-item family of files to see if any other one is also describing something that section doesn't actually say — I only checked the one this step touched.
